title: selection: Implement and test single node hit testing and selection
description: Ensure reliable single-node selection by implementing comprehensive tests and fixes for SEL-001. Addresses Hit Testing & Selection basics.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL accurately determine if a point intersects a node's geometry.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user clicks on an unselected node
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL clear the previous selection and select the target node.

unwanted.condition: IF a user clicks on the empty canvas
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT keep the current selection active
unwanted.because: empty clicks must clear selection as an escape hatch.

postconditions: Selection state contains exactly the clicked Node ID
Visual bounding box is rendered for the selected node

happy: Clicking on a node selects it and deselects others
Clicking empty canvas clears the selection
error: Selecting a non-existent node ID returns an error
Attempting selection with invalid coordinates is rejected gracefully

phase_1: Write ATDD tests for single selection
phase_2: Fix bugs in hit testing and selection state

external_references: Clarification: Assumes node locking status is handled correctly. Hit testing must consider z-index.

title: selection: Implement and test marquee and multi-selection
description: Implement robust multi-selection using Shift-click and Marquee dragging, validating against SEL-002 and SEL-003.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL support selection of multiple nodes simultaneously.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user Shift-clicks an unselected node
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL add the node to the current selection.

unwanted.condition: IF a node is only partially inside the marquee bounding box
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT select the node

preconditions: Target nodes must be fully initialized and present in the document
postconditions: Selection state contains all newly selected nodes in addition to previously selected ones
Selection geometry is re-evaluated to encompass all selected nodes
invariants: Selection bounds must precisely enclose all selected nodes

happy: Shift-click toggles selection status of node without clearing others
Marquee drag selects all fully contained nodes
error: Marquee drag with zero width/height does not crash the system
Selecting out of bounds areas safely returns empty selection

phase_0: Review current multi-select and marquee logic
phase_1: Create comprehensive test cases for marquee containment math

title: selection: Implement and test transformations on multiple selected nodes
description: Guarantee multi-selection transformations (drag, resize) operate collectively without breaking relative geometry (MUL-001 to MUL-015).

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL apply translation offsets equally to all selected nodes.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN multiple nodes are selected and the user drags them
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL move all nodes by the same delta AND preserve relative positions.

unwanted.condition: IF scaling multiple nodes would result in a node size below the minimum threshold
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT scale the nodes beyond that limit
unwanted.because: nodes must remain visible and interactable.

preconditions: Selection set is non-empty for group operations
postconditions: Relative positions between selected nodes are strictly maintained
Edge endpoints for edges between selected nodes remain valid
invariants: Delta transformations are mathematically identical for all entities in the selection group

happy: Dragging 5 selected nodes moves them precisely by dx, dy
Resizing a multi-selection scales all elements from the appropriate anchor point
error: Group resize blocked when attempting to make width/height negative
Empty selection group operations return SelectionError::EmptySelection

phase_1: Implement bulk node position update logic
phase_2: Verify edge endpoints re-computation after move

title: clipboard: Implement reliable copy and paste for isolated nodes
description: Serialize selected nodes, write to clipboard, and paste with newly assigned unique IDs.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL serialize the current selection state completely into a clipboard payload.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user pastes from a populated clipboard
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL deserialize, re-assign IDs, and persist as new entities.

unwanted.condition: IF a user pastes while the clipboard is empty
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT modify the document
unwanted.because: there is no valid data to instantiate.

postconditions: Pasted nodes have NEW unique IDs
Pasted nodes become the new selection
invariants: Clipboard data is self-contained and serializable

happy: Copying and pasting a single node creates a visually identical duplicate with a new ID
Ctrl+D duplicate shortcut immediately clones the selected node with an offset
error: Pasting corrupted clipboard payload returns ClipboardError::InvalidData

phase_0: Define JSON schema for clipboard payload
phase_2: Integrate with OS clipboard via backend API

external_references: Clarification: OS clipboard integration may require specific Dioxus plugins.

title: clipboard: Implement edge ID remapping during clipboard paste
description: When pasting nodes connected by edges, remap the internal edge source and target IDs correctly so they reference the newly pasted nodes, not the originals.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain internal structural integrity of copied graphs.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a copied selection containing internal edges is pasted
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL remap the source and target references to the new node IDs.

unwanted.condition: IF a copied edge references a node that was not copied
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT include that edge in the paste operation
unwanted.because: dangling edges violate the DAG constraints and domain rules.

preconditions: Clipboard payload contains valid edges with resolvable source and target within the payload
postconditions: Pasted edges reference ONLY pasted nodes
Internal graph structure is isomorphic to the copied selection
invariants: No edge points to a NodeId that does not exist in the document

happy: Copy/paste two connected nodes duplicates both nodes and the edge connecting them correctly
Pasting a subgraph with multiple internal connections preserves all topology
error: Copying an edge without its source node drops the edge from the clipboard payload
Malformed edge remapping table during deserialization rolls back the paste transaction

phase_0: Build ID translation map during deserialization
phase_1: Filter out edges missing source or target in the payload
phase_2: Apply mapped IDs to all pasted edge models

title: history: Stabilize basic undo/redo functionality for document state
description: Ensure basic mutations generate a valid history stack and that undo/redo perfectly restore previous and next states.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL support an undo/redo stack bounded to at least 100 entries.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user undoes an action
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL restore exact previous document state from the history stack.

unwanted.condition: IF undo is called with an empty undo stack
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT change the document state
unwanted.because: there is no previous state to restore.

preconditions: Undo stack non-empty for undo operation
Redo stack non-empty for redo operation
postconditions: New document mutation clears the redo stack
invariants: Undo/redo is a perfect inverse function mathematically
History entries are immutable after being pushed

happy: Undo after node move restores original position
Redo after undo restores the moved position
error: Undo with empty stack gracefully returns HistoryError::NothingToUndo
Redo with empty stack gracefully returns HistoryError::NothingToRedo

phase_2: Enforce clearing of redo stack on new actions

external_references: Clarification: Assumes full document snapshots are memory efficient enough for MVP

title: history: Implement history entry batching for continuous drag operations
description: Fix the issue where every frame of a drag operation creates a history entry by batching mutations until interaction completes.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL treat continuous drag interactions as a single atomic history event.

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a continuous interaction mode (like dragging) completes
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL push exactly one snapshot to the undo stack.

unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT pollute the undo stack with intermediate frame-level states
unwanted.because: undo must reverse logical user intent, not physical mouse movements.

preconditions: System correctly tracks interaction state machine (Select -> DraggingSelection -> Select)
postconditions: Only the final state after mouse-up is committed to the history stack
The initial state before mouse-down is preserved as the previous history entry
invariants: A single user intent action maps to exactly one undo stack level

happy: Dragging a node over 60 frames results in only 1 new history entry
Undo after a drag immediately resets the node to its pre-drag position
error: Aborting a drag (e.g. hitting Esc) does not create any history entry
Network disconnection mid-drag does not corrupt the history stack

phase_0: Introduce transaction start/commit markers for interactions
phase_1: Update drag handlers to only commit state on `mouseup`
phase_2: Write tests to verify stack size before and after drag
